summary: Receives FreeD camera tracking data over the network and outputs camera position, rotation, focus, zoom, user, and camera ID channels.
key_concepts: Reads device-independent FreeD camera tracking over the network and exposes CHOP channels suitable for driving a virtual Camera COMP.
Outputs camera_id, tx, ty, tz, rx, ry, rz, focus, zoom, and user channels from the incoming FreeD stream.
FreeD is documented as an older, lower-precision interchange protocol without lens distortion data, so Stype or Ncam may be preferable when hardware supports them.
Only the FreeD D1 camera position and orientation message is processed; other FreeD message types are ignored.
Camera ID filters multi-camera streams, while a blank Camera ID displays whichever camera packet was most recently received.
Protocol, Network Address, Network Port, and Local Address determine UDP or multicast reception on multi-NIC systems.

key_params.name: protocol
key_params.note: Network protocol, such as UDP messaging or multicast

key_params.name: port
key_params.note: Network port to receive FreeD packets

key_params.name: localaddress
key_params.note: Local NIC/IP address to receive on

common_gotchas: FreeD is an older interchange protocol; prefer hardware-specific protocols such as Stype or Ncam when precision and lens data matter.
FreeD In CHOP only processes the D1 camera position/orientation message; other FreeD message types are ignored.
If Camera ID is blank, the CHOP displays whichever camera data arrived last.
Focus and zoom are arbitrary 24-bit units whose meaning depends on the sending hardware.
Multi-NIC systems should set Local Address explicitly to avoid listening on the wrong interface.
